sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Morristown?
sections.html:
Morristown is the county seat of Hamblen County and the largest city in the Lakeway Area of East Tennessee. A sale here involves two sets of offices: city hall for city tax and code questions, and the Hamblen County courthouse for the assessor, trustee and Register of Deeds. Part of the city also reaches into Jefferson County, so confirm which county your parcel sits in before you call anyone.

The Census Bureau estimates 33,517 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 10.2 percent from the 2020 base. The median value of owner-occupied homes is $181,100, so a few thousand dollars of repairs is a meaningful share of what a house can bring.

sections.h2: Where does Morristown sit and how did it grow?
sections.html:
The city lies in the Tennessee Valley between the Great Smoky Mountains to the south and Clinch Mountain to the north. Cherokee Lake, a TVA reservoir built in the 1940s, is just north of town. Gideon Morris and his brothers received land grants here in 1787, and the community was incorporated in 1855 at the crossing of two stagecoach routes. The East Tennessee and Virginia Railroad reached it in 1858, and Hamblen County was created in 1870 with Morristown as its seat.

Industry shaped the modern city. The American Enka rayon plant opened in 1947 and closed in 2005, and the city later built three industrial districts, the last near Interstate 81 exit 8. Furniture maker Berkline, which had been in town since 1937, closed in 2011.

sections.h2: Who employs people in Morristown and what does that mean for buyers?
sections.html:
Morristown is a manufacturing center. A 2021 survey by the area chamber of commerce listed these as the largest employers, and manufacturing is reported to employ about 24 percent of the Hamblen County workforce.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show about Morristown homes?
sections.html:
The latest QuickFacts figures, covering 2020 to 2024, describe a modest-priced housing market:

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 54.9 percent.
  • Median gross rent: $882 a month.
  • Median household income: $47,917.
  • Households: 12,282, at 2.52 people each.
  • Persons in poverty: 26.0 percent.
  • Land area: 27.62 square miles.

Owner costs are low, with a median of $1,177 a month for owners who carry a mortgage and $450 for those who do not. A buyer who plans to rent the house will compare your price against that $882 rent figure.

sections.h2: How do East Tennessee seasons affect a Morristown house?
sections.html:
Morristown has a humid subtropical climate that is slightly cooler than the western half of the state because of its elevation of about 1,300 feet. July highs average 85 degrees, January lows sit near 28, and annual precipitation runs between 44 and 48 inches depending on the record used. Relative humidity averages about 70 percent, and light snow comes occasionally in winter.

That mix of moisture and freeze cycles puts stress on exterior wood, rain gutters, roof flashing and crawl-space vents.

sections.h2: How do Morristown city taxes and Hamblen County taxes work?
sections.html:
City and county each collect their own bill. The City of Morristown mails notices at the end of September. Anyone who pays in October gets a 2 percent discount, and everyone has until the following February 28 to pay with no penalty or interest. The City Tax Office in City Center is open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays, there is a drop box in the City Center garage, and payment cannot be made by phone.

Hamblen County property tax is paid to the Trustee in the courthouse or at the county satellite office at 2415 North Davy Crockett Parkway, and online through TNPayments.com. County tax is due October 1 and becomes delinquent March 1. The Trustee's number is (423) 586-6290.

The Assessor of Property, at 511 West Second North Street, builds one assessment roll for both the county and the city. The office handles roughly 32,000 parcels worth over $3 billion in appraised value. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value, per the Tennessee Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: What papers should a Morristown seller collect first?
sections.html:
A short folder saves days once an offer arrives. Gather these before you talk to buyers:

  • Your last city tax receipt from the City Tax Office and your Hamblen County receipt from the Trustee.
  • A copy of your deed, which the Register of Deeds can supply from records going back to 1860.
  • Any permit paperwork for a roof, furnace, water heater or addition.
  • Notes on open complaints with Codes Enforcement, if any.
  • Names and lease dates for tenants, if the house is rented.

Tennessee assessment records reflect ownership as of January 1 of each tax year, so a fall bill can still carry your name after a sale. Settle the split with the buyer in writing.

sections.h2: Can I dispute my Hamblen County assessment?
sections.html:
Yes. The Assessor is the contact point for the county Board of Equalization, which hears appeals on the assessed value of land and buildings. State law has the county board convene on June 1, and the Comptroller's calendar says a further appeal to the State Board is due by August 1, or 45 days after the county board's notice if that is later. Call the Assessor at (423) 586-1852 to learn this year's last day to file.

The new owner receives the next bill, so tell the buyer if you have an appeal pending.

sections.h2: What Morristown code and permit rules apply to a house I am selling?
sections.html:
Codes Enforcement has two officers who investigate every complaint, usually within 24 hours. When they find a violation, the owner is notified by certified mail and given 14 to 21 days to fix it. If the owner does not, the city can cite the owner into City Court or have a contractor mow or clean the lot and place a lien on the property. Ask your title company to search for city liens.

The department lists the work that needs a permit: a new roof or windows, gas, electrical, plumbing and HVAC work, additions, sheds, carports and pools deeper than 24 inches. Building Inspections can be reached at (423) 585-4626. Overgrown lots, junked vehicles, holes in roofs and unsafe decks are the usual violations. Living in a camper, shed or other structure not built for habitation is not permitted.

sections.h2: Where is the deed recorded in Morristown?
sections.html: Deeds for Hamblen County go to the Register of Deeds on the third floor of the Administrative Building at 511 West Second North Street, phone 423-586-6551. The office holds records back to 1860 and collects two state taxes, the realty transfer tax and the mortgage tax. The transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the greater of price or value, and the grantee pays it.

faqs.q: When are Morristown city property taxes due?
faqs.a: Notices go out at the end of September, and paying in October earns a 2 percent discount. You can pay without penalty or interest until the following February 28. The Tax Office does not take payment by phone.

faqs.q: Does Morristown have a separate county tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Hamblen County taxes are paid to the Trustee, are due October 1 and turn delinquent March 1. You can pay at the courthouse, at the satellite office on North Davy Crockett Parkway or online.

faqs.q: What if a code violation is open on my Morristown house?
faqs.a: Resolve it or disclose it. Codes Enforcement gives 14 to 21 days to correct a violation, and uncorrected cases can lead to a City Court citation or a lien after city cleanup. Call 423-585-1830 for the status of a case.

faqs.q: Which county office records my Morristown deed?
faqs.a: The Hamblen County Register of Deeds, at 511 West Second North Street, 423-586-6551. If your parcel is in the part of Morristown that lies in Jefferson County, ask which register applies before you submit anything.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to repair my Morristown house before selling?
faqs.a: For a new roof, windows, gas, electrical, plumbing, HVAC work, additions, sheds and pools deeper than 24 inches, yes. Call Building Inspections at (423) 585-4626 before you start so the work does not create a problem at closing.
